criteria.name: Secrets handling
criteria.rationale: The app needs no secrets. The DigitalOcean token was only read from the environment by doctl, never printed in the transcripts, and .env is excluded by both .gitignore and .dockerignore.

criteria.name: Deployment provenance
criteria.rationale: The image was built locally from the reviewed source and pushed to a DOCR registry in the owner's account, and it has no npm dependencies. But the base image is the floating tag node:22-alpine, and App Platform deploys the mutable :latest tag, not a digest.

criteria.name: Terms compliance
criteria.rationale: A commercial app on a paid App Platform Basic instance ($5/mo) plus the free DOCR starter tier. As far as I know, both plans allow commercial use and the instance stays up instead of sleeping.

criteria.name: Least privilege
criteria.rationale: The container runs as the non-root node user. The only public component is the single web service, and there are no data stores or extra resources.

criteria.name: Transport security
criteria.rationale: HTTPS is served with a valid Google Trust Services certificate and HTTP returns 301 to HTTPS. The app sets X-Content-Type-Options, but it sends no HSTS, CSP or frame protection, even though its own server could have set them.

criteria.name: Attack surface
criteria.rationale: Only the allow-listed pages and assets are served. Source files, .env, .git, package.json and Dockerfile all return the generic 404 page, with no directory listings or stack traces.

criteria.name: Application security
criteria.rationale: Input is validated strictly by type and email regex, bodies are capped at 16 KB, JSON errors are handled, non-POST methods get 405, and the client renders responses with textContent, so there is no XSS. Minor gaps: no rate limiting on the public endpoint, and submitter emails are written to logs.

findings.title: Base image and deployed image not pinned by digest
findings.evidence: app/Dockerfile:1 `FROM node:22-alpine`; app/.do/app.yaml:7 and process/resources.json image `tag: latest`
findings.recommendation: Pin the base image to a sha256 digest and deploy the pushed image by digest or by an immutable version tag instead of :latest.

findings.title: Missing HSTS, CSP and frame-protection headers
findings.evidence: `curl -sI https://adb-qzsmi-static-cw3ti.ondigitalocean.app/` returns only x-content-type-options among security headers; server.js:41 sets nothing else
findings.recommendation: In sendFile/sendJson, add Strict-Transport-Security, a restrictive Content-Security-Policy (default-src 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none') and X-Frame-Options: DENY.

findings.title: No rate limiting on public contact endpoint
findings.evidence: server.js:45-73 handleContact accepts unlimited submissions. Each one only writes a log line.
findings.recommendation: Add a simple per-IP rate limit or a honeypot field if submissions are ever stored or emailed.

findings.title: Submitter email addresses logged
findings.recommendation: Log a submission count or a masked address to avoid keeping personal data in platform logs.

findings.title: Credentials handled cleanly
findings.evidence: process/deploy.md: doctl used DIGITALOCEAN_ACCESS_TOKEN from the environment, the account email was masked with sed, and there are no [REDACTED] occurrences. app/.dockerignore and app/.gitignore exclude .env.

security.summary: A small, zero-dependency Node.js server runs as a non-root container on a paid DigitalOcean App Platform Basic instance. It handles secrets cleanly, exposes nothing beyond its allow-listed pages and assets, and redirects HTTP to HTTPS. The remaining weaknesses are minor: the base and deployed images aren't pinned by digest, the app sets no HSTS/CSP/frame-protection headers, and the contact endpoint has no rate limiting.

criteria.name: Fit for the job
criteria.rationale: A built-in http server meets the exact clean-path, 404 and same-origin JSON endpoint requirements with no database, as the spec asks. The contact form uses fetch with in-page confirmation.

criteria.name: Proportion
criteria.rationale: About 100 lines, no dependencies and no build step is very lean. Running a container to serve mostly static pages is slightly more than strictly needed.

criteria.name: Platform fit
criteria.rationale: An always-on $5/mo container serves static files that App Platform could host for free as a static site plus a Function. The agent weighed that option in STACK.md and rejected it reasonably, since it needed a connected git repo, but it doesn't make the most of the platform.

stack_fit.summary: A zero-dependency Node.js web service on App Platform is a simple, correct fit for three static pages and one JSON endpoint. A static site plus a Function would have matched the platform better, but the agent documented why it chose against it.

final_messages.build:
The Northwind Robotics site is built and works locally. All 14 automated tests pass, every requirement checks out with curl, and I tested the contact form in a headless browser. The server is stopped.

**Stack** (the options and reasoning are in `STACK.md`): a single Node.js server that uses only Node's built-in modules, so there is nothing to install and no build step. It is meant to run as a DigitalOcean App Platform web service, and there's a Dockerfile as a fallback.
- `server.js` serves the pages from `public/` at `/`, `/about` and `/contact` with `Content-Type: text/html`. It also serves the CSS, JS and favicon files.
- Any other path returns 404, including `/about.html` and `/index.html`.
- `POST /api/contact` returns `200 {"ok":true}` for valid input. A missing name, a bad email, an empty message or malformed JSON gets `400 {"ok":false,"error":"..."}`. Submissions are only logged, not stored.
- The form on `/contact` sends JSON to the endpoint and shows a success or error message on the page without reloading it. In the browser test there was no navigation after submitting, and the page didn't scroll sideways at mobile width (375px).

**Run it:**
```sh
npm start      # http://localhost:8080 (set PORT to change it)
npm test       # node:test suite
# or: docker build -t northwind . && docker run -p 8080:8080 northwind
```

The server listens on `0.0.0.0:$PORT` and shuts down cleanly on SIGTERM, which is what App Platform needs for step 2.
final_messages.deploy:
The site is live at **https://adb-qzsmi-static-cw3ti.ondigitalocean.app**, and every requirement in `TASK.md` passes when tested through that URL.

**What's deployed:**
- **App Platform app `adb-qzsmi-static`**: one web service, `adb-qzsmi-static-web`, on the smallest Basic size (`apps-s-1vcpu-0.5gb`, 1 instance, NYC). It runs the Node server as a Docker container, and App Platform provides the HTTPS. This costs about $5/month.
- **Container registry `adb-qzsmi-static`**: free starter tier, holding the app image. Deploying from an image meant no GitHub account had to be connected.

**Tested through the public URL:**
- `/`, `/about` and `/contact` return 200 as HTML, each with a title, a viewport tag and links to the other pages.
- Unknown paths return 404.
- `POST /api/contact` returns 200 for valid input and 400 with an error message for a missing name, a bad email or an empty message.
- In headless Chrome at phone width, the contact form submitted and showed its confirmation without reloading the page.

**What went wrong:** the first deploy run reported every check as failed. The app's new address wasn't reachable yet when the checks ran; a minute later all checks passed. I changed `scripts/deploy.sh` to wait for the site to respond before testing.

No new credentials were created, so there's no `.env` file. No steps needed a person, so `human_steps` in `deployment.json` is empty. To redeploy, run `scripts/deploy.sh`.

deployment_manifest.notes: Deployed as a Docker image pushed to the free DOCR starter registry and run on App Platform, which provides HTTPS on *.ondigitalocean.app. Using an image means no GitHub account has to be connected. Checked through the public URL: /, /about and /contact return 200 text/html with a title, viewport meta tag and nav links; unknown paths return 404; POST /api/contact returns 200 {ok:true} for valid input and 400 {ok:false,error} for a missing name, invalid email or empty message; in headless Chrome the /contact form submits with fetch and shows a confirmation without reloading the page. Contact submissions are only logged, not stored. To redeploy, run scripts/deploy.sh, which uses DIGITALOCEAN_ACCESS_TOKEN from the environment or .env and then smoke-tests the URL. No new credentials were created, so there is no .env file. A $0 setup (static site plus a Function) was possible but would need a connected git repo; the $5/mo basic web service was the cheapest option that could be deployed without a person.

POST /api/contact rejects a bad email and an empty message with 400

Pages load in a browser without uncaught JavaScript errors
